source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Perform the procedure independently because an RN license automatically establishes competence for every procedure that may be assigned in a hospital.","B":"Delegate the procedure to assistive personnel because delegation transfers responsibility for determining whether the procedure is within the nurse's competence.","C":"Recognize the limitation, review applicable policy, and obtain qualified supervision or competency validation before performing the procedure.","D":"Refuse to learn the procedure permanently because unfamiliarity with a skill means the RN can never perform it within professional practice."}}
source_row.rationale: The current NCSBN test plan places recognition of one's limitations, use of appropriate resources, and practice within legal scope under Management of Care. Option C protects the client while allowing the nurse to obtain the supervision or validation needed before performing an unfamiliar procedure. Option A confuses licensure with demonstrated competence. Option B improperly shifts the issue to assistive personnel. Option D treats a current competency limitation as a permanent prohibition.
source_row.source_detail: 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan — Management of Care, Legal Rights and Responsibilities, printed p.22: recognize limitations of self and others and utilize resources; provide care within the legal scope of practice. The plan measures safe entry-level nursing practice. 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan effective 2026-04-01 through 2029-03-31; official NCSBN/NCLEX source currentness rechecked 2026-08-15. NCSBN first-check: Client Needs — Safe and Effective Care Environment — Management of Care: continuity/transfer of care, collaboration, legal/regulatory scope, quality improvement, leadership and professional-practice activities as applicable. 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan; effective 2026-04-01 through 2029-03-31; currentness rechecked 2026-08-15.
source_row.stem: A newly licensed RN is asked to perform an unfamiliar procedure and has not completed the facility's required competency validation for it. The client is stable. What should the nurse do?
